summary: Install-time host exfiltration, persistent daemon, and cross-tenant node_modules injection
details: The package's package.json declares preinstall and postinstall hooks that run probe.js on npm install. probe.js gates on a cwd matching /tmp/AC<32hex>/ (a Twilio Functions build container layout) and POSTs the output of `id`, a directory listing of /var/task, /proc/<ppid>/cmdline, and AWS_LAMBDA_LOG_STREAM_NAME to a hardcoded webhook.site URL read from hook.txt. probe.js also copies daemon.js to /tmp/.h1poc-daemon.js and spawns it detached with process.execPath (stdio ignored, unref'd), recording pid/version in /tmp/.h1poc.pid and /tmp/.h1poc.ver and SIGKILLing any prior instance, establishing a persistent background process in the shared build container. daemon.js polls /tmp every 100ms for sibling AC<32hex> directories belonging to other tenants, enumerates their service/package subpaths, and POSTs `seen` events (account id, service, package name, foreign flag) plus heartbeats to the same webhook.site endpoint for 15 minutes. daemon.js additionally writes a synthetic `h1-poc-marker` package (package.json + index.js) into node_modules of matched sibling build directories, injecting a package into other tenants' dependency trees during their builds.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
